g.text: Where It Lives in the Diagram
Circle / Sphere — primordial perfect form, infinite symmetry
The entire circular disc (poloidal cross-section); the geometric ring’s “Curved” half is its direct emanation.
Dimensional Ladder — 0D Point → 1D Line → 2D Surface → 3D Solid
Concentric rings: Nucleus (0D), Atom (1D), Algebraic (2D), Geometric disc + Physics Quadrants (3D).
Solids of Revolution — cylinder, cone, sphere, spheroid, paraboloid
Sub-category within ② Conic & Quadratic Curves (rotated conics produce solids).
The “Discrete” half (A–H) — regular polygons inscribed in the circumscribed circle.
Category C (Regular & Semi-Regular Polyhedra) — Platonic, Archimedean, prisms, antiprisms.

text.tspan: All shapes are deviations of circle / sphere

g.text: The entire ring — further from centre = more specific / “deviated” geometric category.
Implicit in figurate numbers ( E ) and the wave-harmonic branches;
the “musical chord of primes” is a harmonic series on the circle ( category ① ).
The nucleus contains π = 14 and b = 3 as the sole fixed axioms (derived from base-3 uniqueness).
The triple (p, q, r) = (7, 11, 13) is a canonical worked example only — any pairwise distinct primes could serve.
The framework does not hard-code 7, 11, 13 — they appear throughout the mapping only as an instance.

Canonical File Address Scheme · plain decimal counting · zero is never used as a digit
Format: <L> . <G> . <O> __ <name>.rs · three positions, every one is a positive integer, zero never appears anywhere
L = Layer number (1..9) · G = Group within layer (counts up, skips any number containing a 0) · O = Ordinal within group (same skip-zero counting)
Files sharing the same L.G prefix are siblings — adjacent on disk, loaded together, related by purpose.
L = 1 → Nucleus · axioms · constants · invariant register
L = 3 → Algebraic · GF(3) · ℤ[φ] · Borromean · Coprime + Bezout · Walk · CRT
L = 4 → Calculi · Δ · ∮ · ◯ · Σ · unified · repx · bijective_converter · SQL planner/executor
L = 5 → Geometric · ring of figures (curved + discrete sectors share one G axis)
G · Group (count up, skip any number with a 0)
For L=5 Geometric the group axis splits in two:
G = 1 .. 7 → curved sectors ① ② ③ ④ ⑤ ⑥ ⑦
G = A .. H → discrete sectors A B C D E F G H
Every other layer (1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9) uses plain numeric G.
See the full Per-Layer Group Atlas below — every occupied (L.G) prefix in the codex.

UX Extension · appended after L.G.O · classifies module purpose for tooling, search, and routing
Format: L . G . O . UX{p} . {s1} . {s2} ... __ <name>.rs · UX is a fixed literal · {p} is one primary digit (1-9) · at least one sub-tag digit must follow (use 1 if none apply)

Triad parallelism: SQL parse @ L=1 (any daemon) → plan @ L=4 (any daemon) → execute @ L=4 with GF(3) batches striped across T-/T0/T+ → storage I/O @ L=8 (router-pinned). Clients only ever speak to T0. T0 dispatches to T-/T+ via the work-steal queue. Every module is reachable by every daemon.
Daemon binary: cargo build --release --features daemon → array3d.exe + libaasc.dll
End-user runs 3 instances: array3d --instance=T- array3d --instance=T0 (gateway · public IPC bound here) array3d --instance=T+ · installer registers all three as Windows services.

Crate Layout · Enforcement · Distribution — one crate, flat layer dirs, local-disk repo, no GitHub required
1. Single crate · flat layer folders · folder code = file's leading L digit
algeometric-arc-sigma182-calculi/ (one crate · one Cargo.toml · one canonical map)
├── Cargo.toml features = { default = [], daemon = ["std","tokio","rayon"] } (no "bridge" feature — crate is trit-pure)
├── scripts/check_ux_tags.sh enforces L.G.O.UX file rule + folder-code rule
├── docs/aasc_canonical_map.{svg,png} ← THIS DOCUMENT (ships with every release)
├── src/lib.rs pub mod L1__nucleus; pub mod L2__atom; ... pub mod L9__physics_nw;
└── src/ flat — no group subfolders (use SQL on Tier-4 GUI for grouping views)
├── L1__nucleus/ 1.x.x.UXp.s__*.rs (constants · milesian · greek_atomic · upiid · units · axes · cone_point · sql_ast · sql_types)
├── L3__algebraic/ 3.x.x.UXp.s__*.rs (gf3 · zphi · borromean · coprime · walk · crt · bezout)
├── L4__calculi/ 4.x.x.UXp.s__*.rs (delta · circular · iteration · series · calculus · repx · bijective_converter · sql_planner · sql_executor)
├── L8__physics_sw/ 8.x.x.UXp.s__*.rs (crystal · lattice · SQL storage · KV · Array3 daemon at 8.7 / 8.8 / 8.9)
2. Three-layer guard (commit · build · CI) — scripts/check_ux_tags.sh asserts BOTH rules
RULE B (folder ⇄ file): parent_dir = L{X}__* ⇒ basename MUST start with X.
a) .git/hooks/pre-commit blocks commit on violation b) build.rs emits cargo:warning= at the start of every cargo build c) local CI (act / woodpecker) runs the guard on push
3. Distribution — three pull paths, all keyed off your local disk, NONE require GitHub

Path 1 — Bake-into-MSI (offline): cargo build --release --features daemon → array3d.exe + libaasc.dll → Installer Framework manifest bundles them → end-user installs MSI → T-/T0/T+ registered as 3 Windows services.

Path 2 — Pull-over-Relay (live signed update): your dev box acts as origin via existing WebSocket relay (same channel that already does GGUF chunked transfer) → end-user daemon polls, fetches, verifies TL-DSA-87 signature, hot-swaps.

Path 3 — Local cargo registry (Tier-3 dev consumers): run kellnr or static-file registry on your box → domain crates declare aasc = { registry = "plenumnet", version = "..." } → no GitHub anywhere in dependency chain.
4. Tier stack — daemon binary is the SAME crate built with --features daemon

Tier 1 = aasc engine (this crate, this map) ← Tier 2 = Salvi domain crates (tdns · tl-dsa · tl-kem · sponge-385 · tis-27 · plenumdb · ttc · ninjaexec · ops-relay · watchdog) link aasc with daemon feature
Tier 3 = JS/React GUI apps talk over HTTP/WS to the Tier-2 binaries; SQL queries on Tier-4 GUI replace any need for group-level subfolders (e.g. SELECT * FROM modules WHERE layer=8 AND group=9).

Net effect: address scheme is mechanically enforced at three independent layers (commit · build · CI); folder names carry the L code so every path is greppable; daemon ships from same source tree under feature flag; T0 is the sole public attack surface; T- and T+ are firewalled internal workers.
Distribution to end-user machines runs entirely off your disk through the Installer + Relay you already have. NO GitHub anywhere in the build, ship, or update chain.
